justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 less-breaking base-design alternative is needed because the R6 invariant preserves the Range shape and appears to broaden or clarify validation rather than invalidate R4-valid instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping the R4 direct comparison would improve old-validator behavioral continuity but would preserve less precise handling of missing values, Quantity comparability, and precision boundaries.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R6 makes the existing ordering invariant explicit about value presence, Quantity comparability, and precision-aware boundaries while leaving `Range.low` and `Range.high` cardinalities and types unchanged. On the available StructureDefinition evidence this is not a hard R4-to-R6 base-design break; the main cost is validator/runtime behavior for edge cases and reverse-version compatibility. Because no official rationale or validator comparison was available locally, `Probably justified` is more appropriate than an unqualified `Justified`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: This is not a backward-compatible-alternative case in the primary R4-to-R6 direction because the R6 base design already preserves the R4 structural content model and is not expected to reject ordinary R4-valid ranges. Retaining the R4 expression as the normative error rule, or adding the R6 expression only as a warning, would mainly preserve legacy validator behavior; it would not better preserve R4 instances and would fail the R6 goal of making range ordering precision- and comparability-aware. R6-to-R4 conversion rules or old-validator shims are useful mitigations, but they are not less-breaking base R6 designs.
